description: Get User information from Active Directory
releaseNotes:
A lightweight Active Directory utility library for .NET that supports forest-wide searches across all domains, flexible LDAP filters, and DTO-based results with access to all Active Directory attributes.

      ✅ Async
      ✅ Forest-wide search
      ✅ DTO-based results (no SearchResult leakage)
      ✅ JSON-friendly
      ✅ NuGet-ready
      ✅ Windows-only (Active Directory)

      Search Active Directory across all domains in a forest.

      ✅ SearchAttribute
      - UserName
      - FullName
      - FirstName
      - LastName
      - All

      ✅ FilterType
      - Contains
      - StartWith
      - EndsWith
      - Is

      ✅ ObjectClassFilter
      - User
      - Group
      - Computer
      - Contact
      - OrganizationalUnit
      - Container
      - Domain
      - PrintQueue
      - ServiceConnectionPoint
      - PublicFolder
      - AllType

      ✅ Returns DTO objects instead of raw AD objects
      ✅ Access all AD attributes dynamically
      ✅ Easy JSON serialization

      🔍 Search users by LastName (using await in WinForms / desktop apps)

      using RPutilities.ActiveDirectory;
      using static RPutilities.ActiveDirectory.Options;

      var users = await ActiveDirectorySearch.Search(
      "Patel",
      ObjectClassFilter.User,
      SearchAttribute.LastName,
      FilterType.Is,
      CancellationToken.None);

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      var s = user.Properties["mail"]?.ToString();
      }

      🔍 Search users across all supported search attributes (using await in WinForms / desktop apps)

      var users = await ActiveDirectorySearch.Search(
      "Patel",
      ObjectClassFilter.User,
      SearchAttribute.All,
      FilterType.Is,
      CancellationToken.None);

      🔍 Search users by UserName (for web apps / sync usage)

      using RPutilities.ActiveDirectory;
      using static RPutilities.ActiveDirectory.Options;

      var users = ActiveDirectorySearch.Search(
      Search,
      ObjectClassFilter.User,
      SearchAttribute.UserName,
      FilterType.Is);

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      var s = user.Properties["mail"]?.ToString();
      }

      🔍 Search users across all supported search attributes (for web apps / sync usage)

      var users = ActiveDirectorySearch.Search(
      Search,
      ObjectClassFilter.User,
      SearchAttribute.All,
      FilterType.Is);

      ✅ Access common properties

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      Console.WriteLine($"{user.DisplayName} ({user.SamAccountName}) - {user.Domain}");
      }

      ✅ Access any Active Directory property

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      if (user.Properties.TryGetValue("mail", out var email))
      {
      Console.WriteLine($"Email: {email}");
      }
      }

      ✅ Handle multi-valued properties (example: memberOf)

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      if (user.Properties.TryGetValue("memberOf", out var groups)  groups is object[] values)
      {
      foreach (var group in values)
      {
      Console.WriteLine(group);
      }
      }
      }

      ✅ Serialize to JSON

      using System.Text.Json;

      string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(
      users,
      new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true });

      Console.WriteLine(json);

      Access the above properties like this:

      foreach (var user in users)
      {
      richTextBox1.AppendText(
      $"FirstName: {user.Properties["givenName"]}\n" +
      $"LastName: {user.Properties["sn"]}\n" +
      $"Employee ID: {user.Properties["employeeID"]}\n");
      }

      Notes:
      - Common AD fields are mapped to strongly typed DTO properties.
      - All returned AD attributes are also available in the Properties dictionary.
      - Multi-valued attributes are returned as arrays.
      - Binary attributes such as thumbnailPhoto are preserved.
      - Common AD date/time fields are converted to DateTime where possible.
      - Domain is populated from the domain search context, with ADSPath parsing as fallback.
